previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis, hepatitis C, and coronary artery disease, was admitted with acute chest and epigastric pain, following an episode of syncope. Initial evaluation ruled out acute coronary syndrome due to normal troponins and EKG. Elevated lipase and clinical presentation confirmed acute pancreatitis, likely alcohol-induced, with gallstones considered less likely given imaging findings. He was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, and analgesia, then advanced to a low-fat diet. His pain stabilized, and he tolerated oral intake. A transient cough resolved with PRN albuterol. Hypertension was managed with an increase in lisinopril from 20 mg to 40 mg daily. He remained stable, with no signs of alcohol withdrawal. He was discharged home with instructions to maintain a low-fat diet, abstain from alcohol, continue home medications, and follow up with primary care and hepatology.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  Chest pain and intoxication.

COMPARISONS:  ___ and ___.

FINDINGS:  PA and lateral chest radiographs.  The lungs are clear.  There is
no pleural effusion or pneumothorax.  The thoracic aorta is tortuous and
stable from ___.  The cardiomediastinal silhouette is otherwise normal.

IMPRESSION:  No acute cardiopulmonary process.

INDICATION:  History: ___ with ETOH, fell on right arm and hit head  // ? R
thumb fx, R forearm fx? brain bleed

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial MDCT sections were obtained through the brain
without administration of IV contrast. Coronal and sagittal reformations, and
thin slice bone algorithm reconstructions were reviewed.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS: 

There is no evidence of hemorrhage, edema, mass effect, or large territorial
infarction. Prominent ventricles and sulci are compatible with age-related
volume loss. Periventricular white matter hypodensities are consistent with
chronic small vessel ischemic disease. The basal cisterns appear patent and
there is preservation of gray-white matter differentiation.

A defect in the left frontal bone is likely post-surgical.  No acute fracture
identified. The visualized paranasal sinuses, mastoid air cells, and middle
ear cavities are clear.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  No intracranial hemorrhage or acute calvarial fracture.

2.  Left frontal bone defect is likely post-surgical.  Please correlate with
clinical history.

EXAMINATION:  CHEST (PA AND LAT)

INDICATION:  History: ___ with ETOH, fell on right arm and hit head  // ? R
thumb fx, R forearm fx? brain bleed

TECHNIQUE:  Chest PA and lateral

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS: 

Heart size is normal.  The mediastinal and hilar contours are unchanged, with
the aorta again appearing tortuous. The pulmonary vasculature is normal. Lungs
are clear.  No pleural effusion or pneumothorax is seen. There are no acute
osseous abnormalities.

IMPRESSION: 

No acute cardiopulmonary abnormality.

INDICATION:  History: ___ with ETOH, fell on right arm and hit head  // ? R
thumb fx, R forearm fx? brain bleed

TECHNIQUE:  Right elbow, three views, right forearm, two views, right wrist,
three views, right hand, three views.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS: 

Within the right elbow, no acute fracture or dislocation is identified. A
joint effusion is not seen. There are minimal degenerative changes within the
elbow joint. No concerning lytic or sclerotic osseous abnormalities.

Within the right forearm, there is no fracture. No focal lytic or sclerotic
osseous abnormality is seen. There are no radiopaque foreign bodies or soft
tissue calcifications.

Within the right wrist and hand, there is a nondisplaced comminuted fracture
involving the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb with intra-articular
extension to the first MCP joint. Diffuse soft tissue swelling is noted about
the fracture. No dislocation is identified. Mild to moderate degenerative
changes are noted involving the first CMC and first IP joints with joint space
narrowing and osteophytic formation. There is no concerning lytic or sclerotic
osseous abnormalities.

IMPRESSION: 

Nondisplaced comminuted fracture involving the base of the proximal phalanx of
the thumb with intra-articular extension.
